National income thresholds are useful starting points, but they obscure a critical reality: the cost of living varies so dramatically across the United States that the same income places you in different classes depending on where you live. Pew Research's cost-of-living adjusted data reveals just how stark these differences are.

A household earning $150,000 in Jackson, Mississippi — where the cost of living is roughly 83% of the national average — has purchasing power equivalent to about $180,700 nationally. That same $150,000 in San Francisco, where costs run about 180% of the national average, has purchasing power equivalent to only $83,300 — technically middle class by Pew's national definitions.

This explains why so many households earning $150,000 to $200,000 in coastal cities feel middle class despite technically being upper-income by national standards. They are not wrong — their lived experience of housing costs, childcare, and taxes genuinely consumes their income at the same rate as middle-income households in lower-cost areas.

Income class and wealth class are not the same thing. The Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances reveals that high income does not automatically translate to high net worth. Many upper-income households carry large mortgages, student loans, and car payments that consume much of their earnings. Meanwhile, some middle-income households with high savings rates accumulate substantial wealth over time.

The FI community lives in this gap. A household earning $90,000 that saves 50% of their income and invests consistently will have a higher net worth within 10-15 years than a household earning $250,000 that saves 5%. Income determines your ceiling; savings rate determines your trajectory. This is why ChooseFI focuses on savings rate and investable net worth as the primary metrics of financial progress — not income class labels.

The financial independence community occupies a unique position in the income class framework. Survey data from FIRE-focused communities suggests the median household income among FI seekers is roughly $130,000 to $160,000 — placing most in the upper-middle-class to lower-upper-income range. However, successful FI stories span the entire income spectrum, from teachers earning $55,000 to tech executives earning $500,000.

What distinguishes FI community members from their income peers is not what they earn but what they keep. While the average upper-middle-class household saves 8-12% of income, FI-path households in the same income range typically save 40-60%. This results in net worth accumulation that dramatically outpaces their income class peers.

The lesson from this comparison is that income class labels describe your earning power, but they say nothing about your financial trajectory. A middle-income household on the FI path will typically surpass the net worth of upper-income households who spend freely. The FI framework redefines "class" around financial freedom rather than consumption — your class is determined not by what you can afford to buy, but by how many years of expenses your investments can cover.

Income class definitions use household income, which combines the earnings of all adults in a home. This creates a nuance worth understanding: a dual-income household where each partner earns $75,000 has the same household income ($150,000) as a single-earner household at that level, but the dual-income household often faces higher total costs (two commutes, potentially more childcare) and different tax treatment. When evaluating where you fall, always use your total household income before taxes and compare to thresholds adjusted for your household size.

The distinction between wealth and income is the foundation of financial independence. Your income class describes your present earning power. Your net worth describes your accumulated financial freedom. The FI community's central insight is that you can move from any income class to financial independence by controlling the gap between what you earn and what you spend — and investing the difference consistently in low-cost index funds over time.

Whether you are middle class, upper middle class, or upper class by any definition, your path to financial independence depends on one number: your savings rate. A middle-income household saving 50% of their income will reach FI decades before an upper-income household saving 5%. Focus on growing the gap between what you earn and what you spend — the class label takes care of itself.

Add up all pre-tax income for your household — wages, self-employment, investment income, and any other sources. Compare to the Pew thresholds adjusted for your household size. For a three-person household, middle income is $56,600 to $169,800.

Use a cost-of-living calculator to adjust your income to the national equivalent. A $120,000 income in a city with 130% cost-of-living has the same purchasing power as $92,300 nationally. This adjusted number is a more honest reflection of your class position.

Your net worth — assets minus liabilities — is a better indicator of financial health than income alone. The median net worth for upper-middle-class households is roughly $465,000. If you are above that with a lower income, you are wealthier than your income class suggests.

Divide your annual savings (including employer retirement contributions) by your gross income. The national average is under 5%. The FI community targets 40-60%. Your savings rate is the single most important predictor of when you will reach financial independence.

Multiply your annual spending by 25 to find your FI number (based on the 4% safe withdrawal rate). Then use your current savings rate and existing net worth to estimate how many years until you reach that number. This timeline matters more than any income class label.

According to Pew Research, upper-income households earn more than double the national median household income. For a three-person household in 2026, that threshold is approximately $169,800. However, this varies significantly by location — in San Francisco, you would need roughly $306,000 to have the same purchasing power as $169,800 nationally.

Upper middle class generally describes households in the top 20-30% of earners but below the top 5% — roughly $106,000 to $169,800 for a three-person household. Upper class typically refers to households above $169,800 (top 19%). The top 5% begins at roughly $280,000 and the top 1% at approximately $590,000. These are income-based definitions and do not account for net worth.

By national standards, $200,000 household income places you in the upper-income category (above the $169,800 threshold for a three-person household). However, in high-cost cities like San Francisco, New York, or Boston, $200,000 has purchasing power equivalent to roughly $111,000 to $130,000 nationally — solidly middle class in terms of lived experience.

The Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances shows the median net worth of upper-income households is approximately $805,400. The top 10% of U.S. households by net worth have $1.9 million or more, and the top 1% have $11.1 million or more. Net worth is a more meaningful measure of financial security than income because it reflects accumulated wealth, not just current earning power.

Lifestyle inflation is the primary reason. Many households increase their spending in lockstep with income increases — larger homes, newer cars, private schools, premium vacations — leaving little margin for savings. A household earning $300,000 that spends $290,000 accumulates wealth more slowly than one earning $100,000 that spends $50,000. The FI community calls this the HENRY problem: High Earner, Not Rich Yet.

Pew Research adjusts income thresholds using an equivalence scale based on household size. A single person needs roughly $56,600 to be middle income (the lower bound), while a family of five needs roughly $126,500 for the same standard of living. Larger households need more income to achieve the same class designation because they have more people sharing the resources.

Income class labels provide useful context for understanding where you stand relative to other American households, but they are a poor measure of financial health. Plenty of upper-income households are one job loss away from financial crisis because they spend everything they earn, while many middle-income households on the FI path have built net worth that places them in the top 10% of all Americans. The framework that matters most is not whether you are middle class, upper middle class, or upper class — it is whether the gap between your income and your spending is large enough to build financial independence within a timeline that matters to you. Focus on three numbers: your savings rate, your investable net worth, and your FI number. Everything else is a label that describes your present circumstances, not your financial future.

Yes, I genuinely gasped when the Tin Can press release landed in my inbox this morning, as it is exactly the product I've been searching for.

While I'm committed to a smartphone-free childhood for my children, I empathise with my children's need to communicate with their friends outside of school. They're also a bit young for the best dumbphones, but I still gatekeep my phone, only allowing occasional texting to other parent's phones in order to reach their pals. And I suddenly realised how unfair this is.

When I was nine, as my daughter is now, I was using our landline to call friends every day, honing valuable communication skills, and the lack of a home phone in my house means that my daughter is unable to do the same. As a new product, it's filling a very real gap in family life – and it's beautifully designed as well.

The Tin Can is already available in the US and Canada, and it's now making it to the UK. It runs on Wi-Fi, so no costly extra landline charges on your broadband (the route I was all set to go down), it looks simple to use, is crucially screen-free, and comes in a variety of delicious colours. It also has helpful parent controls, including restrictions like 'quiet time', you can only call other Tin Can handsets (for free), as well as parent-approved numbers (as part of a monthly subscription), and emergency numbers.

Of course, for best results, your children's friends also need to have a Tin Can – so I'm off to convince the parents I know to put it on their Christmas lists.

Pre orders are open for the UK, and it will arrive with you from 30 November.

#9020. European Beauty Standards: Impact on Self-Image and Diversity

Though we see flickers of progress come and go, European beauty standards — which essentially worship white physical features as the best — are still prevailing across popular culture.

Keep reading to learn more about the damaging beauty ideal. Plus, hear from Siena Liggins, an independent artist and songwriter, about how it affects the music industry and what’s necessary for change.

European beauty standards focus on specific physical features, including light skin and eyes, thin bodies and noses, and poker-straight hair, to name a few.

“It’s honestly just a trickle effect of something that just exists in our culture on a very wide scale,” Liggins says about European beauty standards.

The Western ideal defines beauty through thinness and whiteness, something American culture was all about for, you know, ever.

But beauty standards often shift in America, moving from one extreme like the rail-thin “heroin chic” look in the 90s to today’s adoration of big butts and busts, with a focus on exercise.

Still, whiteness remains the most represented ideal, and we still obsess over thin bodies, regularly debating which celebrities may or may not be on weight loss medication.

The impression the European beauty standards leave us with is that those who most closely match the call for light skin and eyes, thin noses, etc., are the best or most attractive people — leaving some people of color to internalize the messaging, resulting in feelings of self-hate.

This Western beauty ideal is not only exclusionary — shutting out Black, Indigenous, Arab, and Asian, Pacific Islander people — but it’s also deeply harmful.

The standard is unmistakably splashed across the entertainment and beauty industries, from not finding your makeup shade to not seeing your features represented in media.

It also penetrates our daily work and play, creating societal issues and difficulty with self-esteem that impacts everything from securing and keeping a job to socializing and education, starting as young as nursery school.

For one workplace example, a 2020 study found that white women or Black women with straightened hair are more likely to land job interviews than Black women wearing natural hairstyles like afros, twists, curls, or braids.

Some of the first research on skin color and self-perception among Black children included “the doll test.” Researchers presented Black children, aged 3–7, with four dolls that all looked the same — except for their skin color — and asked them a series of questions about which dolls were nicest or prettiest and which they liked best.

Two-thirds of the Black children chose the white doll. The test was repeated in a similar way in 2005, with 16 of the 21 preschool-aged Black children selecting the white doll.

Needless to say, the beauty standard also negatively impacts the educational system, romantic relationships, and a slew of other dynamics and environments.

“The reality is that you need people to challenge them if you’re ever going to see anything change,” Liggins says about beauty standards.

She points to “AMERICAN REQUIEM,” one song off Beyoncé’s country album Cowboy Carter.

“She talks about how for things to stay the same, they have to change again,” Liggins explains. Though she believes Beyoncé refers to a hope for peace and healing in the United States, Liggins says this concept can lend to beauty standards.

When it comes to the idealistic view that we put on celebrities and pop culture, Liggins says you have to reimagine what it looks like over and over again. “And what that requires is letting in new people, and it can’t just be from a vanity’s perspective,” Liggins says.

Coupled with who is represented in music videos, Liggins says change is also needed at a gatekeeper level. “It has to be the people who are coming up with the ideas and bringing them into fruition who also have to have diversity, not just a thought but of background, culture, and ethnicity,” she says.

Otherwise, Liggins says, we’ll only continue to see spikes in diversity, making inclusion more of a fad than a serious change.

A truly kids-focused 3D printer, which is accessible and simple to use. It's built fairly well, but comes with some key compromises in regard to size and build complexity. It's a fun toy, and a good introduction to 3D printing for younger children.

Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

I was captivated by the idea of a 3D printer designed for children, so I jumped at the chance to let my nine-year-old try the Funbox. She’s wanted a 3D printer for ages. I’ve held out, partly because of the cost and partly because of the inevitable tide of tiny plastic things that would end up around the house.

The Funbox is a compact, good-looking printer made by Ugee. It's fully enclosed for safety, has a clean air filter, is anti-scald and you can create with just a tap via the app. With Christmas coming up, plenty of parents will be hunting for the right option for their kids, so I want to be honest about whether this is it. Does this compare to the best 3D printers?

The external design is delightful. Ugee has nailed the look for kids: it’s cute, it has minimal buttons and fuss, and mine arrived in baby blue. A pack of stickers in the box lets your child decorate it themselves.

The inside is just as accessible. The build plate is easy to put in place and everything is clearly marked to show you how to get started (although we did make a wrong turn by not actually putting the plate in the first time around as you can see above – oops!).

Loading filament is simple, though it can be a bit fiddly for small fingers. It is pretty much plug and play – setup took me about 20 minutes, and my daughter was able to manage the first print pretty much independently with minimal interference, only some instruction. Bear in mind, the build space is small, so this printer is best for smaller prints. You can keep an eye on your print via the camera, which links to the app – my daughter was fascinated by this part.

Designs come from a marketplace in the Funbox app, available for mobile or tablet. It should be simple to use, but it’s glitchy. On our Huion tablet, the ‘start’ button was hidden behind the notch and there was no way to scroll or move the screen to reach it. That forced us onto the mobile app, which wasn’t ideal when I wanted my daughter to use the printer independently, without borrowing my phone.

For the most part, the Funbox worked as expected. My daughter could pick a print and start it herself, and she really enjoyed the process.

Sign up to Creative Bloq's daily newsletter, which brings you the latest news and inspiration from the worlds of art, design and technology.

The small build volume is the main constraint. Many designs have to be printed in parts and assembled, which is fine if you stick to small prints. For anything more complex, you’ll need to be ready to help with sticking or putting pieces together. It also prints in a single colour at a time.

Most of the toys we printed turned out well, especially single-piece prints with no moving parts. The detail was good, and the results matched what the marketplace listings promised. Highlights include a cat hair comb, a skull and crossbones hair slide and a phone holder, which would hold my phone if it was the right size (note: must check next time).

Functional toys were a different story. We made a couple of fidget toys that couldn’t do their job without breaking. That could be down to the third-party design, or to the filament being too brittle for the purpose. We couldn’t tell which.

That fits what this printer is: a starter machine built for fun, not one that delivers polished, fully functional prints every time.

We haven’t yet tested the AI 3D model builder, which turns your child’s drawing into a printable 3D model. We’ll cover our experience of it in a separate piece.

The Funbox costs $299/£318 but is often on sale for $279/£289. Whether that’s reasonable depends on who you're buying it for.

For my nine-year-old, I’d rather take on the steeper learning curve of a basic ‘grown-up’ printer like the Bambu Lab A1, which I’d expect to give better-quality prints for similar money. It’s less approachable for a child to use alone, but the results would be worth it for her. For a younger child, though, the Funbox’s ease of use and friendly design make a stronger case, and I think they justify the price.

If you want a genuinely child-focused printer, this is a good option. Just be aware you’re trading away print size and complexity.

Choose your designs carefully. Ugee’s own are reliable, but third-party designs from the marketplace are hit and miss.

If your child is at the upper end of the age range (nine to 12), consider a basic printer from one of the adult-focused brands instead. For younger children, the Funbox is the easier fit.

#9017. Foster + Partners creates Area worktable for today's office

Foster + Partners Industrial Design aimed to bring expressive and functional workplace design together in its modular Area table system, created with Spanish furniture brand Kettal.

Designed to be durable and adaptable, Area combines aluminium columns, a panoply of tabletop options and concealed power.

The aluminium columns anchor the design, serving as both structural support and discreet container for power cables and electrical components.

Available in three diameters – 90, 160 or 450 millimetres – and either anodised or powder-coated finishes, they also bring customisable personality to the worktable.

The tabletops, meanwhile, come in shapes ranging from round to triangular and rhomboid and materials including timber, linoleum, melamine and Fenix. For larger conference or feature tables, terrazzo or marble are also options.

“Area is a collection of durable, expressive elements that define workstations and gathering points within a space to support both individual and collaborative work,” said Foster + Partners head of industrial design Mike Holland.

“The development of Area involved finding the right balance between structural performance, flexibility and visual simplicity,” he continued.

“The system needed to accommodate a wide variety of tabletop configurations and working arrangements, while integrating the technical infrastructure required in contemporary workplaces.”

The Area system can be accessorised with lighting or fabric screen dividers, the infrastructure for which is built into the table. Screen dividers attach magnetically at designed points, with lighting used in combination or mounted independently.

Cables are hidden underneath the tabletop within a J-profile aluminium beam that also provides structural support, while concealed grommets provide access to plug sockets and USB-C connections.

Holland told Dezeen that designing these accessories so they could function seamlessly across a range of tabletop configurations was the key challenge of the design process for Area, alongside achieving the desired proportions and textures for the aluminium columns.

To realise their vision for the expansive system, the design team undertook extensive prototyping, including using both one-to-one and full-scale models and augmented reality (AR).

“Working with full-scale models, augmented reality and 3D printing allowed us to understand the relationship between the different components and how they would function together in real working environments,” said Holland.

“This approach was particularly important in refining the columns, assessing their proportions, and adapting the surface texture pattern at full scale. It also allowed us to evolve the design from wider diameters into more elegant and efficient forms.”

He said that working with models and AR also allowed manufacturer Kettal to engage in the design process and contribute ideas.

“Collaboration is at the heart of our approach, and we believe it is fundamental to achieving the highest-quality results,” said Holland.

Area was designed for the contemporary workplace, said Holland, where flexible and hybrid working have made the office primarily a place for collaboration and connection, and where the table’s modularity and adaptability allow it to evolve as needs change.

“As designers, we are interested in the points of interaction between people and buildings,” said Holland. “At the heart of industrial design lies the creation of these touchpoints through which people experience space.”

“In the workplace, furniture plays a vital role in shaping how people engage with their environment, influencing how they occupy, navigate and connect with the spaces around them,” Holland concluded.

Part of the architecture firm Foster + Partners, Foster + Partners Industrial Design started by creating site-specific furniture, fixtures and fittings for the company’s buildings and over the last 50 years have expanded to more stand-alone commercial products.

Some of its recent designs include the Join plywood furniture collection, Ori bird feeders and Datum porcelain tableware.

#9015. Should I Exercise with a Phlegmy Cough? What You Need to Know

You’re feeling a bit under the weather, but you don’t want to lose the momentum of your fitness routine. So, should you push through and hit the gym, or is it better to rest and let your body heal? Let’s break it down!

Sleep is the best way to help your body recover quickly when you’re sick. But if you’re determined to rise and grind, you could use the “neck check” to decide whether to lace up those sneakers or stay in bed.

Many sports doctors use this theory to say that if your symptoms are above the neck — sniffles, sore throat, or a mild headache — you’re generally good to go for a light workout. But if you’re dealing with chest congestion, a hacking or juicy cough, diarrhea, a fever, or an upset stomach, it’s better to take some time to catch up on your Netflix watchlist.

Big disclaimer: there’s little scientific evidence behind the “neck check,” so use your best judgment.

If you’re going with the above-the-neck rule, exercising with the following symptoms is probably okay.

Going super hard if you have a mild cold is not a good idea. But a light workout, like a walk or a chill Peloton sesh, can be a great way to stay active without overdoing it. Stretching or light yoga might also do the trick.

Stick to light activities like walking for most earaches. Avoid intense workouts like weightlifting, yoga, or pilates, as they can throw off your balance and put pressure on your sinuses, exacerbating the pain.

Light and short workouts are likely fine if your sore throat is mild and lacks fever, cough, or swallowing issues. Remember to stay hydrated — it can ease your sore throat and is beneficial during exercise.

Light activities like brisk walks or gentle bike rides can help for allergy-related stuffy noses. If your nose is blocked, stick to very light activities, focusing on breathing. Skip workouts if you have a fever, chest congestion, or a productive cough with phlegm until you’re symptom-free.

If you’re experiencing the following symptoms, the workout can wait.

Working out with a fever increases dehydration risk and can worsen the fever. Plus, fever saps your muscle strength and coordination, making you more prone to injuries. So, do yourself a favor and skip the workout until you’re back to normal.

An occasional cough is your body’s way of clearing out irritants, but a frequent or phlegmy cough could signal a respiratory infection like a cold, flu, or even pneumonia or asthma. While a tickle-induced cough isn’t a gym deal-breaker, a persistent one is.

Diarrhea and vomiting can dehydrate you, and physical activity only makes that dehydration worse. Feeling weak? That’s a recipe for injury. Plus, stomach bugs are highly contagious. If you feel antsy, stick to light stretching or yoga at home.

The flu hits your respiratory system hard, with symptoms like fever, chills, sore throat, body aches, fatigue, headache, cough, and congestion. If you’ve got the flu, take it easy and give your body some well-earned R&R.

Once symptom-free, ease back into exercise gradually. Start with less intense workouts to avoid overdoing it. As your symptoms fade, you can gradually return to normal activity.

Regular exercise may shorten recovery time, particularly for acute respiratory infections. Listen to your body’s signals to gauge your strength. If you’re still contagious, opt for home or outdoor workouts, so you don’t spread those germs to fellow gym-goers.

It's my favourite Apple design in decades

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I remember my first Apple product. It was the fourth generation iPod – the last model to feature a monochrome screen. For a few years I'd backed the wrong horse, thinking Sony's minidisk players were the future of portable music. But as soon as I held the iPod, I was smitten. It felt like it had fallen out of the future, and like it was designed just as much to be looked at as it was to be used. And for the first time in decades, I'm feeling the same way about a new Apple product.

After a week with the iPhone Duo, I'm, well, smitten again. After years (and years) of incremental upgrades, we finally have something that feels genuinely new and exciting. And if you can swallow the huge asking price, I think this might be the ultimate smartphone for creatives.

I'll be exploring how the iPhone Duo fares for specific creative tasks over the coming weeks, but today I want to talk specifically about the design. This thing feels truly luxurious. With its gleaming metallic finish and satisfyingly compact proportions when closed, it reminds me somewhat of a vintage cigarette holder. There's something almost Art Deco about it. Foldables have always felt awkward, but Apple has somehow made it elegant.

Speaking of size, I've seen plenty of online commentators complain that the Duo is too small (Apple is even rumoured to be working on a larger version). But for me, it's perfect. As someone who prefers phones that don't require three hands to hold, I've always been one of the few defenders of the iPhone mini. For me, its diminutive dimensions are precisely the point. After years of phones getting progressively more enormous, there's something wonderfully refreshing about a device that actually wants to fit in your pocket.

But of course, the real headline here is the larger internal display. This has been the subject of debate too, thanks to the matte nano-texture layer. This does take some getting used to (and in my experience, seems a little harder to clean), but there are massive benefits too – namely, vastly reduced glare. And perhaps even more importantly, it makes the dreaded 'crease' less visible.

There are some delightful software touches that make the Duo a joy to use. The open/close animation, which blurs content as the screen is folded or unfolded, is subtle way of explaining that content is moving from one screen to another. And my personal favourite touch is the new StandBy mode, which works when the phone is propped in 'tent' mode, turning it into a desk calendar and clock.

As a creative, the possibilities of the Duo are immediately appealing. Having more room to view images, browse design inspiration or work with visual content without reaching for a separate tablet feels like a meaningful improvement, rather than another feature invented to fill a keynote. I'll be exploring the creative potential in more detail soon. But for now, after just a few days with the device, it's clear that Apple's sense of fun is well and truly back. This is a bold yet playful product design that feels, for the first time in forever, like it has fallen out of the future.

#9013. Does Creatine Increase DHT? What You Need to Know

Ah, creatine! It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance. But as you’re hitting the gym harder and seeing results, there are some potential side effects to be aware of. Here’s the lowdown.

Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells. It helps to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) — your muscles’ go-to fuel when working hard.

Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements. Why? Because more creatine equals more ATP, which means more energy for high-intensity activities. More fuel means more mileage!

Now, here’s where things get hairy. You might dial up your body’s DHT (dihydrotestosterone) production when you uplevel creatine. DHT is a derivative of testosterone and plays a big-league role in developing male characteristics. But here’s the catch: while DHT might beef up your alpha vibe, it’s also notorious for thinning out hairlines in peeps predisposed to male pattern baldness.

So, do creatine supplements cause baldness? Maybe! The buzz mainly stems from a small 2009 study where college-aged rugby players loaded up on creatine and saw their DHT levels increase significantly.

Because DHT can shrink hair follicles and shorten the hair growth cycle, it may seem logical to blame creatine for contributing to hair thinning. However, it’s important to remember that these findings are a one-hit wonder — they haven’t been seen again in other studies. Plus, let’s not forget that intense workouts alone can pump up these hormones, too.

As a result, the jury’s still out, making the creatine-and-baldness saga a hot topic for gym gossip and scientists alike.

The same 2009 study found that after a week of taking high-dose creatinine at 25 grams per day, DHT levels rose by 56%. When the researchers dropped the dose to 5g daily for two more weeks, levels remained 40% higher than baseline. These findings contrasted with the control group participants who took a placebo.

Does this mean creatine could spell disaster for your do? Well, creatine boosts DHT, the usual suspect in male pattern baldness, also called androgenic alopecia. However, your disposition to hair loss and the effects of DHT is genetic, meaning that it’s inherited.

Some folks are more prone to DHT’s hair-ruffling effects because of how their androgen receptor gene is wired. Hormones like testosterone and DHT bind to androgen receptors, typically triggering normal hair growth. However, variations in the AR gene make the androgens extra effective, making you more likely to experience hair loss.

So, while there isn’t much evidence to say that creatine supplements cause hair loss, the connection to increased DHT levels is worth considering if your family reunions look like a convention for bald eagles.

Beyond the potential for a breezy scalp, creatine is actually solid in the safety department, with long-term studies giving it a thumbs up. However, although creatinine doesn’t pose a risk to healthy individuals, it might not be your best move if you have kidney, high blood pressure, or liver disease.

Another thing to keep in mind is that creatinine loves to hang onto water, so expect some extra bloat and weigh-in surprises as your body adjusts.

Thinking of starting a creatine kick? Chatting with your doctor first is always wise, especially if you have other health conditions or take medications. They can advise you and rule out any potential interactions.

If you’re taking creatinine and notice changes to your hair, a check-up is a good idea. Shedding a few strands is normal, but it’s a red flag if you start losing clumps of hair. Rapid hair loss can indicate underlying health issues that go beyond your hairstyle.

Furthermore, consult a doctor if hair loss is weighing on your mind. They can offer solutions or treatments to manage your hair loss and stress.

Creatine is celebrated for its muscle-building prowess, but rumors of a link with hair loss exist. The good news is there’s little conclusive evidence directly connecting creatine supplementation to permanent hair loss.

However, creatine loading may boost DHT levels, a hormone linked to male pattern baldness, especially in people genetically predisposed to hair thinning.

So, if you’re concerned about hair loss, it might be wise to talk with a doctor before adding creatine supplements to your muscle-building routine.

#9012. Pepper & Well designs bathroom that mimics concrete architecture of Paul Couch house

Melbourne-based studio Pepper & Well took cues from crisscrossing concrete walls and ceiling beams when designing Lumeah, a new en-suite for a house by celebrated architect Paul Couch.

Located in Macedon, central Victoria, the linear single-storey house was completed in 2006 by the late Couch, who passed away earlier this year.

When new owners bought the property in 2018, they felt the layout and finishes of the main bathroom didn’t meet the standards of the rest of the house.

They asked Pepper & Well to upgrade it and make it more accessible.

“There was an opportunity to make the space more comfortable and practical as they aged,” said lead architect Andy Dal Pozzo.

The previous layout included a WC, an enclosed shower and a step-in plunge pool, all within a space just 3.5 metres long.

Pepper & Well’s scheme removed the plunge, allowing space for a larger WC and for an open shower to be built in place of the old frosted-glass enclosure.

The defining move was the addition of a cast-concrete element that partitions the toilet and shower areas.

This incorporates an informal bench, allowing for seated showers if preferred.

The geometry of this element clearly references the house’s exposed concrete structure, a rhythmic arrangement of concrete beams over concrete walls.

“Our approach began with understanding the logic of Paul’s work,” explained Dal Pozzo.

“We wanted the renovation to share the original architecture’s material honesty and clarity, while remaining recognisable as a new contribution,” he said.

A change in floor surface marks the junction between old and new.

While most of the room features the bluestone flooring installed 20 years ago, the toilet and shower have a surface of crazy-paved slate.

The stone is the same Mintaro Brown Back slate that Couch installed in the bathroom of his own house, Toolern Vale.

“Laid in crazy paving beside the retained bluestone, it introduces a distinct texture with a direct connection to Paul’s work,” said Dal Pozzo.

The rest of the room was left largely intact, including the solid timber doors and the vanity unit spanning the opposite wall.

There are subtle correlations between the two sides of the room, so as not to make the new insertion feel disparate. For instance, a glass screen matches the height of the mirror opposite.

The shower also includes a stainless-steel handrail that doubles as a towel rail, matching the rest of the bathroom fixtures.

“The scale of the commission demanded close attention to every decision, from the arrangement of the room to the meeting of two stones,” added Dal Pozzo.

“By revealing the original fabric, retaining what worked and introducing a few carefully resolved elements, we sought to give the clients a bathroom that would serve them into the future and continue the architectural story of their home.”

Lumeah is shortlisted for bathroom of the year in Dezeen Awards 2026.

Other projects in this category include Kan Atelier’s design for the William King Apartment, a residence in a 1950s block in Athens, which won the public vote.

You might be suffering whiplash if you've been watching things at Etsy lately. Just a couple of weeks ago, things looked tentatively hopeful for the marketplace as Etsy promised to crackdown on AI slop. Now creators are fleeing the platform in droves because of its own AI policy.

Creators have largely welcomed Etsy's decision to ban listings by bots and to insist that product photos resemble the actual product being sold – surely a rule that all marketplaces should implement. But new wording in its terms of use has caused alarm over how content could be used for AI training. As a result, the best website builders could be about to see an influx of custom from artists and crafters.

A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration)

A post shared by Cognitive Surplus (@cognitivesurplus)

A post shared by aaron meshon (@aaronmeshon)

A post shared by Elena Skoreyko (@elenaskoreyko)

A post shared by Leanne (@snackhungrycreations)

A post shared by Elisa | Kunst & Design fresh from the forest (@hohwald_atelier)

A post shared by Vanessa 👩🏻 (@little_inkdrops)

A post shared by StayKpopPrints (@staykpopprints)

For years, Etsy has been one of the best places to sell art and design online, particularly handmade craft items, from jewelry and gifts made with Cricut machines to illustration and poster design. But like many platforms, it's faced the problem of quality products being drowned out by AI slop and copied art posted by bots.

Shortly after updating its content rules to try to get on top of that, Etsy's also updated its Terms of Use. The new text adds a clause that has echoes of the policies introduced by certain social media platforms.

The new terms come into effect on 16 December, and they've sparked an exodus from the platform. Many creatives have taken to social media to announce the closure of their Etsy stores, using flyers and goodbye letters created in their signature art styles.

Some speak of wrestling over a decision that they fear could harm their business in the short term. Others who have yet to take the leap say they feel trapped because they depend on Etsy as their main source of income and the update has come at the most important time of the year for sales.

Sign up to Creative Bloq's daily newsletter, which brings you the latest news and inspiration from the worlds of art, design and technology.

Like with Cara for social media, alternative specifically anti-AI marketplaces like Marmalade Handmade, but they remain small compared to Etsy. Some sellers say they can't leave the platform yet but are taking the step of writing to customers to ask them to shop with them directly instead of using the platform.

In an update on the Etsy Community site this week, VP of Customer Operations James Ossman stressed that sellers retain ownership of their creative work on Etsy that the company was focusing on using AI to support sellers and improve the Etsy experience.

He writes: "We do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity. Again, this is not changing. Our goal at Etsy has always been to connect you and your unique items with buyers."

He provided some examples of how the platform is training AI, including to identify potentially fraudulent accounts and related listings, to understand inventory, to help buyers find items and tailored recommendations and to build tools to help sellers run their businesses more efficiently.

He said Etsy uses security tools to detect and limit unauthorised scraping, while its terms prohibit unauthorised use of marketplace content for AI training. However, he doesn't specify whether authorised partners can use seller content to train models for applications unrelated to Etsy, and the platform has not provider a general opt-out mechanism for sellers who don't want their content used for AI training.

It may be that sellers have nothing to fear, in which case Etsy should really have tried to find a better way to communicate the update. It's aware of the sensitivity around AI, and it's natural for sellers to be frightened by the language in the new terms at a time when AI is being used to clone artists' work in a multitude of fields, from illustration to video game development.

Are you concerned about Etsy's AI policy? Let us know in the comments.

#9010. Is Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) Worth It? The Hidden Costs

Buy Now Pay Later services let you split a purchase into installments — typically four payments over six weeks (Afterpay, Klarna "Pay in 4") or monthly payments over 3-36 months (Affirm, Klarna financing). The checkout process is seamless: enter your name and email, get instantly approved, and walk away with your purchase having paid only the first installment.

BNPL providers make money in two ways. First, they charge merchants 4-8% of each transaction — significantly more than the 2-3% credit card processing fee. Merchants accept this because BNPL increases average order values by 30-50%. Second, some providers charge interest on longer-term plans, and nearly all charge late fees when you miss a payment.

The "interest-free" label on short-term plans deserves scrutiny. While you may not pay interest, the behavioral cost is substantial. Research from multiple financial studies shows that BNPL users spend 30-50% more per transaction than they would with cash or debit. The psychological separation of the purchase from the full payment removes the natural spending brake that keeps budgets in check.

The financial industry has known for decades that separating the moment of purchase from the moment of payment increases spending. Credit cards exploit this. BNPL takes it further by making the payment feel even smaller — "just four easy payments of $37.50" feels dramatically different from "$150" even though it is the same amount.

A 2026 survey found that 43% of BNPL users have missed at least one payment. Among those who missed payments, the average person missed three or more over the prior year. Late fees compound quickly — four missed $8 Afterpay fees on a $200 purchase adds $32, effectively creating a 16% surcharge on what was supposed to be interest-free.

The credit score impact is evolving rapidly. As recently as 2022, most BNPL activity was invisible to credit bureaus. That has changed. Affirm now reports all payment activity to Experian and TransUnion. Afterpay reports to Equifax. Klarna reports financing plans to all three bureaus. On-time BNPL payments may slightly help your score, but missed payments can drop it significantly — and the damage lasts up to seven years.

For anyone pursuing financial independence, BNPL represents the opposite of the FI mindset. FI is built on intentional spending, high savings rates, and letting compound growth work in your favor. BNPL encourages impulsive spending, fragments your cash flow, and creates obligations that reduce your ability to invest.

There is exactly one scenario where BNPL is financially rational: a planned, budgeted purchase at 0% interest where you would have paid the full price regardless. For example, you need a new dishwasher, you have the $800 in savings, and the retailer offers four interest-free payments. You keep your $800 invested for six more weeks while paying in installments. The benefit is tiny — a few dollars of investment returns — but the cost is genuinely zero if you make every payment on time.

Outside this narrow scenario, BNPL is almost always a worse choice than the alternatives.

The financial independence community is nearly unanimous: BNPL is a trap disguised as convenience. The entire BNPL business model depends on you spending more than you planned. If you were going to buy the item anyway and you have the cash, just buy it. If you do not have the cash, that is your budget telling you something important.

The question to ask before any BNPL checkout: "Would I buy this right now if I had to pay the full price in cash today?" If the answer is no, BNPL is not helping you afford something — it is helping you overspend. If the answer is yes, just pay cash and skip the installment tracking, the payment reminders, and the risk of a missed payment damaging your credit.

For those building toward financial independence, every dollar matters. The 30-50% spending increase that BNPL encourages directly reduces your savings rate — the single most important variable in determining how quickly you reach FI.

The average ChooseFI listener saves $24,000+ with an expert student loan plan.

Trusted by Brad Barrett, Co-founder and Host, ChooseFI

Mortgage lenders are increasingly scrutinizing BNPL obligations during the underwriting process. Multiple active BNPL plans — even if interest-free — show up as recurring liabilities and can affect your debt-to-income ratio. If you are planning to apply for a mortgage or auto loan in the next 6-12 months, pay off all BNPL balances and avoid opening new ones. Lenders view fragmented installment obligations as a sign of cash flow stress, even if you have never missed a payment.

Affirm is a legitimate, publicly traded company (AFRM on NASDAQ). It is safe in the sense that it will not steal your money or identity. However, being legitimate does not mean it is a good financial decision. Affirm's interest rates range from 0-36% APR depending on creditworthiness, and the company reports all payment activity to credit bureaus.

Increasingly, yes. Affirm reports to Experian and TransUnion. Afterpay reports to Equifax. Klarna financing plans report to all three bureaus. On-time payments may help slightly, but a single missed payment can significantly damage your score and remains on your report for up to seven years.

Afterpay charges an $8 late fee per missed payment, capped at 25% of the order value. After multiple missed payments, your account is suspended, the balance is sent to collections, and the delinquency is reported to Equifax. Collections accounts damage your credit score severely and remain for seven years.

Klarna's "Pay in 4" plan is interest-free with no late fees, but your account may be suspended for missed payments. Klarna's longer-term financing plans charge 7.99-33.99% APR, involve a hard credit pull, and report to all three credit bureaus. Read the terms carefully — the word "Klarna" covers very different products.

It is possible but unlikely for most people. Research consistently shows that BNPL increases spending by 30-50% per transaction. If you have the discipline to use BNPL only on planned, budgeted purchases at 0% interest — and never miss a payment — the financial harm is minimal. But for most users, the behavioral cost exceeds any convenience benefit.

Because it works — for the store. Merchants pay BNPL providers 4-8% of each transaction (vs 2-3% for credit cards) because BNPL increases average order values by 30-50% and reduces cart abandonment by 20-30%. The merchant is paying for you to spend more. That should tell you who this arrangement benefits.

Buy Now Pay Later is a marketing innovation designed to make you spend more — and the data confirms it works. BNPL users spend 30-50% more per transaction, 43% miss payments, and the credit reporting implications are growing. The only responsible use case is a planned, budgeted purchase at 0% interest where you already have the cash. For everyone else, especially those pursuing financial independence, BNPL is a detour in the wrong direction. Pay with cash, invest the difference, and let compound growth work for you instead of against you.

#9009. 10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:

Caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future plans feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

If imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love plans a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

If they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

If your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024

#9007. B2 Architecture turns North Korean defector testimonies into Prague exhibition

Photography by Radek Šrettr Úlehla

B2 Architecture has created the Life Behind the Walls exhibition in Prague, using a maze of red timber frames and translucent fabric to explore life in North Korea.

The 1,500-square-metre exhibition takes visitors from a bright, interactive installation designed around a children’s book to a darkened gallery featuring portraits and testimonies from North Korean defectors.

B2 Architecture divided the installation into two contrasting environments. The first features a grid of red-painted timber beams, with large sheets of red and pink fabric suspended between the frames to create semi-transparent walls.

The structure forms a maze that visitors can explore, with glimpses of other rooms and activities visible through the fabric.

Illustrated panels, games and interactive activities are fitted into the structure, while photographs by photographer Michal Huniewicz show North Korea as it is presented to the outside world.

Children are encouraged to navigate the maze independently and stop to draw, write and complete activities as they move through the installation.

The displays are based on Tota lítá, a children’s book by North Korean studies scholar and writer Nina Špitálníková, which explains the principles of totalitarianism in language that is accessible to younger readers.

“Children are often given very little space within exhibition formats,” B2 Architecture told Dezeen. “This project consciously challenges that convention.”

The atmosphere changes as visitors pass between two walls displaying photographs of the border between North Korea and China by photographer Tim Franco.

Beyond this threshold, the playful red maze gives way to a dark gallery. This contains black display structures with portraits and personal accounts of people who escaped North Korea, alongside stories of those who did not survive its regime.

Tall, translucent fabric panels printed with shadowy human figures were arranged throughout the space, creating silhouettes that overlap with the portraits displayed behind them.

In a central room, a monumental statue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un stands on a raised plinth, surrounded by spotlights and theatrical mist.

The temporary installation was constructed using lightweight, modular timber beams and stretched textiles, allowing it to be assembled and dismantled efficiently.

The timber structure was retained for use in another project, while the textiles and flooring were passed on to several theatres for reuse.

Prague-based B2 Architecture was founded by architect Barbara Bencová in 2012 and works across residential and commercial architecture, interiors and public spaces.

Other projects by the studio featured on Dezeen include the DDB Prague office, which features an anamorphic optical illusion that makes the advertising agency’s logo appear complete from a particular viewpoint.

#9006. Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home.

Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up!

Why are my ears clogged?

Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked:

  • Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage.
  • If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection.
  • Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side.
  • Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too.
  • Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure.

Best clogged ear remedies

1. Pop and unclog

The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes.

2. Swallow, yawn, or chew

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow.

3. Ear drops

Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes.

Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful.

4. Warmth and gravity

To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily.

5. Hit the steam room

Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 

6. Take allergy medication

Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears.

Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort.

7. Rinse away the gunk

Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing.

When to see your doctor

Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention.

What not to do when you have clogged ears

  • Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. 
  • Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries.
  • Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion.
  • Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation.

Takeaway

Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies.

PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 is a worthy upgrade to its predecessor, cleverly interlinking back and lumbar systems so you're completely supported as you move around in the chair. It's still not the most attractive of chairs, and assembly could be more straightforward, but once it's up and running, you'll find levels of ergonomics that actually belie its $499.99 / £459.99 price.

Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

Chairs seem to come in pairs. I've been getting a lot of chairs in for review recently, with the remarkably similar Secretlab Titan Evo and the DXRacer Martian Pro showing up around the same time. Now, having just reviewed the Boulies EP600, the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 has taken my focus – and they have so much in common, it’s like they were separated at birth.

The design of the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 is almost a mirror image of the Boulies EP600: Both feature curvy three-piece back panels with responsive lumbar supports, pull-out footrests, and they’re roughly the same price. But where the Boulies EP600 was feature-packed and poorly executed, the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 nails the execution, and it’s definitely one of the best office chairs for back pain. It’s also a marked improvement on its predecessor, the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro.

Like most of Sihoo’s chairs, the Doro C300 Pro makes use of mesh throughout. There’s nothing wrong with that: mesh makes chairs lighter and easier to pack, but it lacks the sink-in sumptuousness of cushioned chairs, including its own budget-friendly Sihoo M18.

However, where the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro gets everything absolutely right is in its engineering. While it can feel a little clunky and firm to start with, once it’s dialled-in it reaches astonishing levels of comfort with the versatility to move around and change positions.

This begins with the lumbar support, which naturally moves and follows your lower back as you lean backwards and forwards. Unlike the aggressive system in the Boulies EP600, it flows with you and never becomes intrusive.

Sihoo also includes a sacral support system here, which cradles the heart-shaped sacrum bone at the base of your spine with a gentle pressure I’ve never felt before. It’s one of the best lumbar systems I’ve used, and it’s adjustable so you can hone it just as you want it.

The lumbar support moves alongside the rest of the chair as you shift around; lean back and the armrests follow the backrest and the seat cushion moves forwards. It's always got your back (literally), and it delivers on the promise that the automated Hbada X7 failed to deliver, and it does so without motors or AI.

Sign up to Creative Bloq's daily newsletter, which brings you the latest news and inspiration from the worlds of art, design and technology.

Endless adjustments don’t end there: the armrests can also be tweaked and rotated to optimise your comfort levels, apparently through eight dimensions. This sounds like it might break the very fabric of reality, but if I’m going to implode with an alternative-dimension version of myself, at least I can do so with comfortable elbows.

One neat feature here is that the rear portion of the armrests flips up and locks into place, giving you a little more comfort when you’re reading, sketching, or diving back into another 16-hour GTA VI binge, and the (optional) mesh leg rest also helps you relax into a state of utter relaxation as you cause chaos in Vice City.

Sihoo reckons the chair will suit anyone up to 6’ 3”, and it fits my 6’ 4” height perfectly, with the headrest in just the right place. Sihoo has also upgraded the weight accommodation to a maximum of 136 kg, so this is a chair that can be used by pretty much anybody and everybody.

Beren’s take on the original C300 Pro was that it was one ugly motherfu…rniture. The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 doesn’t break the mould in terms of looks, and it’s almost indistinguishable from other ultra-adjustable ergonomic office chairs: it’s the Boulies EP600, it’s the Hinomi H2 Pro.

These chairs tend to be triumphs of function over form, although I’m not sure anyone outside of Gold's Gym will have shoulders wide enough to justify the upper width of the backrest. Where they differentiate themselves is in the view from the back.

The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 looks reasonably attractive: the headrest’s large “eyes” and its nose-like supports actually recall Gonzo a little bit, while the armrests, in grey, have a friendly cetacean look about them. It’s still not the best-looking chair, but these touches add a playfulness that reduces its dour, generic design.

Choosing the grey colourway Sihoo sent us also helps lighten the heaviness of the design and stops it looking like a predatory black blob in front of your desk.

Take note: this is a herculean, 27kg chair that comes in two boxes, and not something you’ll want to be moving vertically once assembled. Within one of those boxes you’ll also find my pet peeve with Sihoo chairs: having to put the base together and insert those 10 screws. I’ve done it countless times and it never gets easier or more fun. It makes me think about my own mortality.

Sihoo’s assembly process is nowhere near as straightforward as, say, Branch’s. There is a fair amount of cross-referencing to be done between the manual, the screw blister-pack, and the chair itself, to the extent that I thought an escape room-style door would open somewhere when I’d completed it. The armrests connect via washers that seem a little too big for their holes, and they take a bit of brute force to get them in place.

Sihoo has kept the number of steps involved to the absolute minimum, and when it’s done it feels remarkably sturdy. But the niggling annoyances in its construction do add up, and it feels like there are plenty of opportunities for Sihoo to simplify things. They can start with that wretched base.

Office chair pricing is so complicated and fluid that it can be hard to find a coherent and consistent price, but apparently the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 carries an RRP of $499.99 / £409.99, with the footrest costing an extra $40 / £50, but these prices are often discounted. The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V1 was a frankly absurd RRP of $699 when Beren reviewed it; thankfully, Sihoo seems to have made its pricing more sensible since then.

Is it worth it? I’d say a definite yes; despite my grumbles about the construction process, this is a comfortable and innovative chair that gets a lot of things right. If you’re torn between the Sihoo Doro Pro C300 V2 and the Boulies EP600 ($489.99 / £429.99) I’d definitely recommend the Sihoo option.

If your budget stretches a little more, then the Hinomi H2 Pro ($ / £759) is a worthy contender, with similar adjustability and a neat folding feature — although it lacks the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2’s versatile armrests. And, of course, there’s the ever-dependable Sihoo M18 (under $ / £200), if you want to spend less but still need a decent level of lumbar support.

Sihoo’s upgrades really do make a big difference with the Doro C300 Pro V2. The way it all works together is a marvel of engineering, and it adds up to one of the best back support systems I’ve ever used. The fact that it achieves it without batteries and motors is impressive in itself. It’s a chair that cradles your back from the moment you sit in it, but that can also be tweaked in just the right ways, without ever becoming overwhelming or overcomplicated.

The biggest downsides here are its chunky looks and its fiddly assembly process, but both of these will evaporate the moment you sit on it. It’s the perfect chair for people who like to move around a lot, and who like to kick back for entertainment in the same chair they work in.

He loves to translate the complex into accessible, whether that with text or video. When he’s not thinking about what creatives need to do their jobs properly, he’s busy discovering new and creative ways to fall off his bicycle.

#9004. Are Tangerines Good for You? 5 Health Benefits You Might Love

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024
